title: Credit Controller
description:
The Credit Controller will handle financial transactions and maintain accurate records to support the accounting and finance department in the retail industry. Based in Brighton, this role ensures the smooth running of financial processes critical to the organisation's operations.

Client Details

This role is within this exciting, growing industry and is based in Brighton.

Description
- Process and reconcile financial transactions in a timely manner.
- Maintain accurate records for all credit-related activities.
- Ensure compliance with relevant financial regulations and company policies.
- Collaborate with internal teams to resolve discrepancies and improve processes.
- Prepare reports and documentation for management and auditors.
- Monitor and manage outstanding balances to reduce risk exposure.
- Support month-end and year-end financial processes.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller should have:
- Experience in accounting or finance within a similar role.
- A strong understanding of financial processes and regulations.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Proficiency in relevant financial software and tools.
- The ability to work effectively within a team and independently.

Job Offer
- A permanent role based in Brighton.
- Salary ranging from 29,000 to 32,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Opportunities to develop career
- In office with hybrid

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. title: Document Controller
description:
Document Controller

Location: Brighton
Job Type: Permanent
Salary: Competitive

We are working with a growing construction business who are looking to appoint a Document Controller on a permanent basis.

The company specialises in cladding remediation projects and is continuing to grow, offering a great opportunity to join a business with a friendly and supportive working environment.

The Role

As Document Controller, you will be responsible for managing and maintaining project documentation, ensuring information is accurate, up to date and distributed to the relevant teams.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing and maintaining project documentation and records
- Uploading, issuing and distributing drawings and project information
- Maintaining document registers and ensuring information is kept up to date
- Managing revisions and ensuring the correct documentation is issued
- Liaising with project teams, subcontractors, consultants and clients
- Supporting the wider project team with document control and administration
- Ensuring company procedures and document control processes are followed

About You

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience working as a Document Controller, ideally within construction
- Good knowledge of document control processes and systems
- Strong organisational and administrative skills
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good communication skills and the ability to work with different project teams
- A proactive and reliable approach to work
- Experience working within construction, refurbishment or cladding would be advantageous

This is a great opportunity to join a growing business specialising in cladding remediation, where you will become an important part of the team and have the opportunity to develop your career within the company.

If this permanent role is of interest, please reach out directly to Charles Howe of Tradeline Recruitment

description:
Exam & Office Administrator

About us

At Aldridge Adult Learning, part of Aldridge Education, we are passionate about changing lives through learning. We provide high-quality education and training that helps adults build confidence, gain valuable skills and achieve their career aspirations. By putting teaching, learning and learner support at the heart of everything we do, we create an inclusive environment where every learner can thrive.

Join us as our Exams and Office Administrator

The aim of the role is to provide high-quality administrative support for learner services, examinations, and office functions across Aldridge Adult Learning (AAL).

The post holder will maintain learner records, coordinate examinations and assessments, support learners and curriculum teams, and ensure compliance with organisational and awarding body requirements.

Working closely with staff, learners, and external partners, the successful candidate will contribute to learner achievement, provide excellent customer service, and support the smooth day-to-day running of the organisation.

Reporting to the Office Manager, the Exams and Office Administrator will work collaboratively across AAL to maintain effective systems and contribute to the organisation's ongoing success and reputation.

We welcome applications from all sections of the community and particularly encourage applications from underrepresented demographics.

About Aldridge Education:

AAL is a member of the Aldridge Education family of schools, which locally also includes BACA, PACA and Dukes.

Aldridge Education is a charitable Trust of entrepreneurial community schools and colleges that help young people to reach their potential. We support our schools Principals and teachers in rapidly improving the quality of education on offer at early years, primary, secondary and sixth-form levels in order to transform the life-chances of our students

title: Finance Assistant (Accounts Payable) - Brighton
description:
Finance Assistant (Accounts Payable) 6-Month FTC Brighton

We're working with a leading organisation in the business services space to recruit a Finance Assistant (Accounts Payable) on a 6-month fixed-term contract. Based in Brighton, this role will play a key part in supporting the day-to-day financial operations of the business.

Working within a collaborative finance team, you will ensure financial transactions are processed accurately, support reconciliations and reporting activities, and help maintain the financial controls that underpin effective business decision-making.

Responsibilities
- Process supplier invoices accurately and efficiently, ensuring all transactions comply with financial controls and approval procedures.
- Review and process employee expenses and company card transactions, maintaining accuracy and compliance with company policies.
- Allocate customer receipts and maintain accurate records to support effective cash management.
- Reconcile supplier accounts, investigate discrepancies, and liaise with suppliers to resolve outstanding issues.
- Complete bank reconciliations, identifying and resolving unmatched transactions.
- Support supplier payment runs, ensuring payments are made accurately and on time.
- Prepare financial information and supporting data for reporting purposes.
- Analyse budget variances and identify trends, risks, and areas requiring investigation.
- Build strong relationships with colleagues and suppliers to resolve finance-related queries promptly.
- Support month-end, year-end, and audit activities.
- Provide flexible support across the finance function as required.

About You
- Previous experience in a finance, accounts payable, or transactional finance role.
- Experience processing invoices and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify and resolve discrepancies.
- Excellent organisational and communication skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and finance systems.
- Ability to manage priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

To be considered for the role, candidates must be available to start the role immediately.

We are happy to provide application and/or accessibility support, please contact your Marks Sattin or Grafton consultant directly to discuss your needs. We're committed to protecting the privacy of all our candidates and clients, please visit and for our privacy policy.

title: Team Administrator
description: Please note that this role is being offered as a Fixed Term Contract for 12 months or as an internal secondment opportunity. We are looking for an organised and proactive Team Administrator to join our busy East Neighbourhood Mental Health Team. This is an important role within the team, providing the day-to-day administrative support that enables our multidisciplinary staff to deliver safe, effective and timely care to people using our service. You will work closely with clinicians and other members of the team, helping to keep the service running smoothly. No two days will be the same, and you will need to be comfortable managing a range of competing priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail in a fast paced environment. You will provide a comprehensive administrative service to the team, including supporting referrals and appointments, maintaining accurate patient and waiting-list information, processing correspondence and clinical documentation, arranging meetings and providing general administrative support to the multidisciplinary team. The role involves working with confidential and sometimes sensitive information, so accuracy, discretion and good communication skills are essential. You will use a range of electronic systems and will need to be confident with IT and able to learn new systems quickly. We are looking for motivated and enthusiastic person who is: Organised; Knowledge of System 1 desirable Have sound IT/administration skills (Word, Excel, PPT); Work well in a team; Have excellent communication skills; Have good interpersonal skills and is able to work in a confidential and sensitive manner. You will be offered opportunities for training and professional development. We would be very happy to discuss any questions or queries with prospective candidates. The Team Administrator will provide a full administrative service, having daily liaison with a wide range of staff at all levels and regular contact with people who use services and their carers, who may at times be distressed or angry. The Team Administrator will be responsible for ensuring the effectiveness of the office environment for the team.
